signoff.summary: Chair review complete. Re-ran ERC, netlist diff, sch_lint, and PDF renders myself from the delivered files (not trusting prior self-reports) and independently confirmed: zero ERC errors on all six new sheets (Emulator MCU, Solar and Sensor Emulation, Solar Power Injection, Battery Replica and Bench Power, Pyro Inhibit and Jumpers, Bench IO); the 11 project ERC errors are byte-identical to the Rev2 FC baseline on both the raw-Rev2 and post-promotion baselines (every error class +0); netlist diff vs tools/baseline/netlist.kicadxml shows 218 components added/0 removed, the only 8 removed nets are the exact brief §4.3 label promotions with membership preserved, and all 30 changed nets are pin-gains only (zero lost pins on any existing net). All 14 chair-ranked fix-now items are applied and I independently reverified each directly in the schematic/netlist: R5 (CHG_SYS now 4x22uF/25V/1210 = 51.1uF effective at 8.4V vs 44uF min), R6 (R600 4.7k sourced from FC +3V3, not 3V3_EMU, resolving a new armed-state hazard the literal ruling would have created), R7 (14 device-side pull-ups 10k->4.7k, Face 0 stays 10k), plus 9 minor documentation/datasheet-conformance fixes and 2 generator-infrastructure items (pantry path decoupled from the session scratchpad; 5/6 generators now uuid-stable) — the latter two were reported inconsistently across two fixer passes, so I independently regenerated all six sheets from a clean environment with no scratch/env vars set and confirmed byte-identical (uuid-stripped) reproduction, twice consecutively, and confirmed zero PCB footprints reference the new refdes ranges (nothing to orphan). Two prior findings (ids 34, 38) are refuted with reasoning preserved in the report. Two items (DRV2605L C303 100nF, Face-0 43ohm dummy load) are accepted with documented rationale. Five ask-hardware-lead items are spelled out with recommended defaults (CSYS same-class DC-bias proxy curve, C511/C515 1210-vs-0805 deviation, R505 bleed resistor, per-channel EN-to-GND header for Phase 2, a firmware wiring question to relay). Full report written to docs/flatsat/2026-09-14_phase1_schematic/02_review_report.md.
for_hardware_lead: CSYS 44uF minimum was met using a same-class KEMET DC-bias proxy curve (C1210C226K3PAC), not the fitted Samsung CL32A226KAJNNNE's own curve (none published); recommend accepting given 16% margin (51.1uF vs 44uF), but add a bench CSYS ripple/derating measurement to the Phase-2 bring-up checklist.

C511 (CPMID) and C515 (CBAT) were upsized to 22uF/1210 instead of the fix item's suggested 22uF/0805, reusing the CSYS BOM line (LCSC C52306); recommend accept unless 1210 footprint area near U511 is a board-space concern for Phase-2 layout.

R505 (battery_protection_replica, 100k bleed resistor on VBAT_BENCH_N) remains a documented deviation from strict battery_pack_v2 fidelity (brief D4), awaiting a PM/hardware-lead ruling; recommend keep it (safer failure mode), electrically inert (84uA at 8.4V).

No per-channel EN-to-GND header exists yet to allow mixing real and emulated face boards (mitigation today is a 'do not plug a real board while emulation is fitted' note, D11); recommend deferring to Phase 2 unless mixed real/emulated bench use is expected before the next layout respin.

Relay to firmware/proves-core-reference owner: ReferenceDeploymentTopology.cpp lines 178-182 pass muxChannel0Device to every drv2605FaceNManager.configure() including drv2605Face5Manager -- if unintentional, DRV2605L traffic for faces 1/2/3/5 would land on TCA9548 ch0 instead and the FlatSat emulator on EMU_F1..F4 would never see it. Not a FlatSat hardware issue either way.
for_layout_phase: Confirm during Phase-2 bring-up that fitted CSYS (Samsung CL32A226KAJNNNE, 4x22uF/25V/1210) actually derates in line with the KEMET proxy curve used to justify the R5 fix -- it is a same-class estimate, not a datasheet-verified number for the exact fitted part.

Outstanding LCSC/supply-chain pass (PM ruling R12, deferred, not a Phase-1 blocker): 8 LCSC numbers need catalogue re-verification, remaining blanks (test points/jumpers/headers) need sourcing, and Datasheet-URL fields are empty on 24 non-passive parts (headers, jumpers, switches, LEDs, L200).

All six tools/gen/*_gen.py generators are now uuid-stable and pantry-independent (verified by the chair from a clean env, byte-identical reproduction twice consecutively), but this was only exercised pre-layout -- zero footprints in FlatSat_V1.kicad_pcb reference any of the six new sheets today. The first post-layout regeneration should be diffed against the PCB's footprint-to-symbol-uuid links before trusting Update PCB from Schematic.

FlatSat_V1.kicad_pro's cached 'sheets' list is stale (Rev2-era, omits the six new sheets) -- cosmetic, regenerates on next GUI save, but do not script against it as a hierarchy source for layout tooling.

Two firmware-side (not FlatSat-hardware) items to resolve before Phase-3/4 HWIL bring-up: DetumbleManager's 13ohm coil-resistance default vs the ~41-43ohm the real board and FlatSat replica actually have, and the drv2605Face5Manager mux-channel wiring question above.

id 38 (claim two emulated channels can fall back to RP2350 hardware I2C slaves to mitigate PIO-engine risk): Refuted -- a hardware I2C slave (DW_apb_i2c) ACKs only one programmed address, while BATT (4x TMP112) and TOP (VEML6031+TMP112) -- the two channels the finding proposes moving -- must answer for two to four distinct slave addresses each, so no hardware-engine fallback exists for them. Recording this as a mitigation in the GPIO map would mislead Phase-3 firmware. No schematic change either way.

21 kept items after merging duplicates from the verified packet (ids 1+22, 4+20, 23+31, 3+33, 25+35 merged into single fix items) plus 2 refuted items dropped with reasoning.

Three PM fix-now rulings (R5, R6, R7) are confirmed NOT YET carried out in the delivered sheets/generators and are ranked 1-3 as major fix-now items, each assigned to its single owning sheet (battery_protection_replica, pyro_inhibit, solar_emulation respectively). Notably, the verifier's own re-analysis (finding 31) surfaced that applying R6 exactly as literally worded (R600 100k->4.7k straight to 3V3_EMU) creates a NEW hazard -- an indeterminate armed-state EN level when the emulator is unpowered during an FC-only deploy/heater test (brief D11) -- so item 2 folds in a rail-source correction (source R600 from FC +3V3 instead) rather than a literal R6 application.

Rank 4 (emulator_mcu note corrections) is a downstream documentation dependency on item 3 landing, and also fixes an independently-verified factual error in the phantom-power note (the AP2112K LDO cannot be relied on to sink 3V3_EMU; the note's claimed mechanism is wrong).

Ranks 5-12 are minor fix-now items: three bench-safety/documentation gaps on pyro_inhibit and battery_protection_replica sheet text (self-contradicting jumper tables, misleading SAFE-LED semantics, missing power-up recipe), a cheap OTG-tie-low datasheet-conformance fix, an optional CBAT/CPMID capacitor bump to ride along with the R5 edit, a GPIO firmware-crosswalk documentation gap, and two cross-repo bench-procedure notes (bench_io USB warning, solar_power_injection test prerequisite).

Ranks 13-14 are tooling/process items on the generator infrastructure (owner_file "root" as integrator-style owner): the pantry dependency on the session scratchpad (verified to break all six generators once the scratchpad is gone) and non-deterministic uuid regeneration in five of six generators (verified to have zero PCB layout exposure today, so pre-layout housekeeping rather than an active bug).

Ranks 15-16 are accept-with-rationale: DRV2605L decoupling value and Face-0 dummy-load resistance both follow the brief's explicit golden-reference-parity instruction, with documented rationale for why the apparent datasheet/firmware-model mismatch is not a FlatSat defect (in the R304 case, independently verified that the FlatSat's 43ohm value actually matches the real PCB coil geometry better than the firmware's 13ohm default, pointing to an upstream proves-core-reference issue instead).

Ranks 17-21 are info/no-action items already covered by existing PM decisions, correctly-deferred R12 (LCSC/datasheet) items, or harmless KiCad cache staleness.

DC-BIAS SOURCE (this is what R5 and item 1 demanded, and it changed the answer). Murata SimSurfing, Samsung Component Library and
TDK's characteristic viewer are JS front ends and could not be retrieved here (probed and recorded in the report). The curves used
are KEMET/YAGEO K-SIM (https://ksim3.kemet.com, the manufacturer's own simulator), "Capacitance vs. Vbias (DC)" at 25 C, exported
as CSV from its plot endpoint:
  C1210C226K3PAC  22 uF 25 V X5R 1210 : -13.44% @5.0V, -41.89% @8.4V -> 12.78 uF      <- same C/V/dielectric/case as C52306
  C1206C106K3PAC  10 uF 25 V X5R 1206 : -12.21% @5.0V, -39.03% @8.4V ->  6.10 uF
  C0805C106K3PAC  10 uF 25 V X5R 0805 : -32.80% @5.0V, -59.99% @8.4V ->  4.00 uF
  C1210C106K3PAC  10 uF 25 V X5R 1210 :  -6.76% @5.0V, -19.08% @8.4V ->  8.09 uF
  C1206C226K4PAC  22 uF 16 V X5R 1206 : -50.39% @5.0V, -70.47% @8.4V ->  6.50 uF
  => CSYS = 4 x 12.78 = 51.1 uF effective at 8.4 V, 16% over the 44 uF minimum of SLUSD88A 9.2.2.3.
     dVSYS = IOUT*D/(fSW*CSYS) = 1.5 A * 0.405 / (1.5 MHz * 51.1 uF) = 7.9 mV (was quoted 17 mV at a claimed 24 uF).
  => The ruling's first suggestion ("add a third 22 uF") does NOT work in 0805 (3 x ~8.8 = 26 uF) and does NOT work in 1206
     (3 x <=12.8 = <=38 uF); the sheet's old "~24 uF" was optimistic - the delivered 2 x 22 uF 0805 held under 18 uF.
     2 x 47 uF 25 V 1210 was rejected because no vendor curve exists for it in any reachable tool and a 47 uF part in the same
     case/rating must derate at least as hard as the 22 uF one - i.e. it would have been the guess the ruling asked us to stop making.

refuted.title: With the inhibit engaged, the HWIL suite cannot observe a burn/heater command: EN nodes move only 0 -> 0.28 V and the emulator has no view of them - use the three free emulator lines to tap the FC command nets
refuted.why: Every electrical statement in the finding reproduces, but the defect it asserts is measured against a requirement that does not exist in the brief or the plan. The plan of record explicitly excludes pyro/deploy testing from the FlatSat ('a separate fixture owns deploy ATP') and runs the HWIL suite 'minus burnwire' / 'excluding pyro tests' in Phase 4, so there is no Phase-4 scenario in which the console must observe a burn command through the emulator; D9's PYRO_INHIBIT_STATE read is a safety interlock ('Sense only'), not an observability requirement; and there is no heater test in the suite at all. The GPIO allocation the reviewer wants to repurpose (SPARE0/1 on the J703 bench header, RSVD test-point-only) is a brief contract decision (sections 4.2, 6.1, 6.6) spanning emulator_mcu, bench_io and the firmware GPIO map, so changing it is a PM amendment, not a fix-stage defect on pyro_inhibit. Nothing here makes the FlatSat not work, unsafe, damaging to the FC, misleading to flight software or unbuildable; the sheet already documents the 0.28 V inhibited level and the DMM verification path. The recommendation as written is also electrically wrong: a 4.7 k series tap into the existing 4.7 k E9 pull-downs (R208/R209/R210) puts the emulator pad at 1.65 V when the FC drives 3.3 V, below the RP2350's VIH(min) of 2.0 V (section 14.9.4 Table 1436), i.e. in the undefined region. Refuted as a Phase-1 finding; keep as an info/idea for the PM and the Phase-4 test plan.

refuted.title: PIO risk mitigation already present in the GPIO map: every emulated channel's SDA/SCL pair sits on a hardware I2C function pair, so two channels can fall back to the RP2350 hardware I2C slaves if the PIO slave needs two state machines per channel
refuted.why: The pin-mux fact is reproducible, but the conclusion does not follow: a DW_apb_i2c slave ACKs exactly one programmed IC_SAR address (address match and ACK happen in hardware before software sees the transaction), while every emulated channel must answer for two to four distinct slave addresses. BATT (four TMP112s) and TOP (VEML6031 + TMP112) - the two channels the finding proposes to move - cannot be served by a hardware I2C slave, so no 'no-respin exit' for the 2-SM-per-channel risk exists via the hardware engines. Recording it in the GPIO map would mislead Phase 3 firmware. Nothing on the schematic changes either way; info at most, and the claimed mitigation is refuted.
